subject: international-relations
intro: International relations leads to the professions around world politics — analysing political systems and conflicts, mediating disputes, working on trade and development, and funding the organisations in between.

roles.title: Political Scientists
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree (most positions require a master's or Ph.D.)
roles.what: Study the origin, development and operation of political systems, analysing public opinion, decisionmaking and ideology, and comparing how governments and other political entities work.
roles.where: The frameworks unit — interests, interactions and institutions — and the institutions, law and norms unit are political science in miniature, and the war unit's regime-type arguments are exactly the comparisons they run.

roles.title: Intelligence Analysts
roles.entry: High school diploma or equivalent plus academy training
roles.what: Gather, analyse and evaluate information from databases, surveillance, intelligence networks and geographic systems, using it to anticipate and prevent organised crime such as terrorism.
roles.where: The civil war and terrorism unit — why insurgencies form and why terrorism happens — is the substantive background analysts apply, and the history of the international system gives the context behind today's threats.

roles.title: Arbitrators, Mediators, and Conciliators
roles.what: Facilitate negotiation and conflict resolution through dialogue, settling disputes between parties outside the courts by mutual agreement rather than by imposed rulings.
roles.where: The bargaining model of war unit explains why negotiations collapse and how they are made to hold, and the institutions and cooperation unit shows the agreements mediators help parties actually sign.

roles.title: Economists
roles.what: Conduct research, prepare reports and formulate plans addressing economic problems in production, distribution and monetary or fiscal policy, often using sampling and econometric methods.
roles.where: The trade, development and environment unit is applied economics — sanctions, growth and climate policy — and the institutions unit's trade agreements are the cooperation problems economists model.

roles.title: Fundraisers
roles.what: Organise activities to raise funds and solicit donations for an organisation, producing promotional material and raising awareness of the organisation's work, goals and financial needs.
roles.where: The human rights unit is where non-governmental organisations live on voluntary money, and the institutions and cooperation unit's coalitions and partnerships are the networks a fundraiser mobilises for development and environment causes.
